svg.title: The GLM-5.3 flagship did not slip: its open weights shipped on Hugging Face on August 28 under a bespoke license whose one substantive departure from MIT is a revenue-gated security review aimed at hyperscalers
svg.desc: A correction-and-resolution diagram. On the left, the previous brief's read is shown superseded: the August 29 brief predicted a slip, reading that August 28 passed with no weights on Hugging Face and no new date. That box is struck through. An arrow leads right to what actually happened: the GLM-5.3 flagship weights did publish on Hugging Face on August 28, 2026 — Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 60, a 753-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts with 40 billion active — but under a custom license tagged glm-5.3, not MIT. A center mechanism box explains the license: its one substantive departure from MIT is a revenue-gated security-review clause — any Model-as-a-Service operator whose affiliated group exceeds 10 billion US dollars of revenue over any consecutive 12 months must pass a Z.AI security review before commercial use; the scope of that review is set by Z.AI. The diagram frames this as governance by license rather than governance by withholding: the summer's held-because-dangerous flagship went open, with a legal gate aimed at the largest cloud operators standing in for a withholding. A two-tier band shows both GLM-5.3 models now open — the flagship at Index 60 under the glm-5.3 license from August 28, and GLM-5.3-Flash at Index 57 under plain MIT from August 26. A footer notes the closed ceiling stayed frozen for a ninth straight brief: Claude Opus 5 at Index 63 is still number one and uncut at 5 and 25 dollars, no Index-64 model and no ceiling flagship price cut since July 24; Gemini 3.5 Pro stays absent on a third missed target; Meta's Watermelon still carries an October date, now paired with a paid Hatch agent platform; and GPT-5.6 Sol's late-August cut to 4 and 20 dollars is a workhorse-tier move below the ceiling, not a new number one.
svg.text: The flagship didn't slip — it shipped open Aug 28, under a hyperscaler-gated license
Correcting the Aug-29 read: GLM-5.3's weights are on Hugging Face. The "danger" gate resolved into a license clause, not a withholding.
AUG-29 BRIEF READ — SUPERSEDED
Flagship GLM-5.3: "a slip"
Aug 28 target passed —
no weights on HF, no new date.
Read as outcome (c): withheld.
actually
SHIPPED — WEIGHTS ON HUGGING FACE
Flagship GLM-5.3, Aug 28 2026
Index 60 · 753B MoE / 40B active · verbose
Downloadable, self-hostable —
license field: glm-5.3 (not MIT)
THE ONE SUBSTANTIVE DEPARTURE FROM MIT — A REVENUE-GATED SECURITY REVIEW
A Model-as-a-Service operator whose affiliated group exceeds $10B revenue over any 12 months
must pass a Z.AI security review before commercial use. Scope of review set by Z.AI.
Governance by license, not by withholding — the cyber-capable flagship went open, with a legal gate aimed at hyperscalers.
Both GLM-5.3 tiers are now open:
Flagship 60 · glm-5.3 license · Aug 28
Flash 57 · plain MIT · Aug 26
HELD — 9TH STRAIGHT BRIEF AT THE CEILING
Closed #1 frozen: Opus 5 · Index 63 · uncut $5/$25. No Index-64 model, no ceiling flagship price cut since Jul 24 (now ~6 weeks).
Gemini 3.5 Pro still absent (3rd missed target; newest is gemini-3.1-pro-preview). Meta "Watermelon" still Oct, now paired with a paid "Hatch" agent platform.
GPT-5.6 Sol's late-Aug cut to $4/$20 undercuts Opus 5 on price — but at the workhorse tier below the ceiling band, not a new #1.
Through-line: the open-weights arc (Kimi=hardware → Qwen=proof → GLM-5.3=danger) closes its last gate as a license, not a lock.
